subject: Forecast-driven slice agreement and demand-signal support
messages:
From: Julia Connors <julia.connors@cobaltlabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 spike — request for a guaranteed slice + forecast attached

Hi Mina / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our Q2 forecast (forecast_q2_demand.xlsx) — we expect a ~4x burst for two 2-week windows: May 10-24 and Jun 7-21 driven by a marketing campaign and a scheduled model retrain that increases inference traffic.

As discussed, we'd like to explore a short-term reserved slice (GPU pool lane) to ensure latency and avoid cold-start variability. Key asks:
- A guaranteed slice (~8 A100-equivalent slots) for the two windows above
- Clear preemption rules if capacity is constrained (how and when you reclaim)
- A way for us to push a demand signal or forecast so Redwood can pre-warm autoscaling or carve capacity proactively

We are open to a cost-sharing model for the buffer. Can you outline feasibility and a rough timeline for approval? I attached our forecast and a one-page suggested commercial term sheet.

Appreciate it,
Julia
Julia Connors
Head of Platform, Cobalt Labs
julia.connors@cobaltlabs.com

--- Attachment: forecast_q2_demand.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet, 124KB)---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Connors <julia.connors@cobaltlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q2 spike — request for a guaranteed slice + forecast attached

Thanks Julia — forwarding internal for feasibility. Quick summary for the team: Cobalt needs a short, high-confidence reserved lane for two discrete 2-week windows (May and June). They want a mechanism to send a demand signal/forecast and ask about preemption behaviour. They are willing to pay a share for the buffer.

Aditya / Evelyn: can we support a forecast-driven reservation workflow without major product changes? Specifically:
- Acceptable guarantee model (hard carve vs soft buffer with guaranteed minimum tokens/sec)
- Preemption semantics + notice window (they asked how we reclaim slots if we get saturated)
- Telemetry / webhook: can external forecasts be ingested to increase pre-warm/batch sizing and/or temporarily raise autoscale target?

Laura / Dev: please prepare an ops and commercial sketch (T&Cs, runbook for on-call, rollback). I attached a short proposed terms stub (proposed_slice_terms.pdf) to start legal review.

I think a 30-min cross-functional sync this week will move this quickly — propose Wed Apr 28 11:00am PT. If you can't make that, flag availability and we'll triage.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
--- Attachment: proposed_slice_terms.pdf (PDF, 48KB)---

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q2 spike — request for a guaranteed slice + forecast attached

Thanks for the context. A few product/engineering constraints to call out so we can scope work:

1) Demand-signal ingestion: we do not currently accept external forecast webhooks into the autoscaler. We can accept a manual upload or an internal ticket-driven override today. Building a secure, authenticated webhook + validation + UI will be ~3-4 sprints (prod backlog) unless we scope a narrow MVP (one-off forecast upload + manual approval).

2) Autoscale override feature: to support pre-warm without breaking global SLOs we'd need a temporary override flag that raises the autoscale target for a named customer slice and allows preemption by system-critical traffic. Implementing a timelimited 'hard carve' that persists across restarts is higher risk and needs infra changes (KV persistence for carve metadata). Est. effort: 2-3 sprints for safe rollout, 1 sprint for narrow internal-only feature flag + monitoring.

3) Alternative quick path: quota-pooling + burst lanes. We can create a soft buffer (not fully isolated) that preferentially serves the customer with documented preemption and a 30-min notice. This requires no infra change and is operationally feasible within 48-72 hours if legal/commercial sign-off is in place — tradeoff is weaker isolation.

Concrete asks for scoping:
- Mina/Dev: confirm whether Cobalt requires hard carve (no preemption) or is OK with preferenced burst lane and 30-min preemption notice.
- Evelyn: if we go with preferenced buffer, can infra reserve N slots and set preemption policy in the runtime? Any obvious conflicts with upcoming cluster maintenance in May?

I'll join Wed's sync and can bring a proposed minimal design doc (PROD-6243) and a short list of telemetry events we need.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q2 spike — request for a guaranteed slice + forecast attached

High level infra note: we have two GPU pools that are at ~78-82% projected utilization across May in our current forecast; cluster maintenance (node firmware updates) is scheduled May 12-14 which reduces available slots by ~10% for that window. Hard carve will be difficult to guarantee across that maintenance unless we pre-stage capacity or move the carve to a different region.

Operational proposal (safe, minimal disruption):
- Implement a forecast-driven preferenced buffer: reserve 8 slots in a burst lane tagged for Cobalt for the requested windows, with preemption allowed and a 30-min notice signal.
- Add a temporary autoscale target bump for the tagged slice at signal ingestion (manual for MVP).
- Ops runbook: who to page, how to reclaim, rollback steps (I will draft).

If customer insists on an unpreemptible carve, we'd need an exception to reassign nodes and shift scheduled maintenance or buy committed capacity for the month (finance/legal approval required).

I'll run a quick capacity simulation and attach the result to the sync.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
--- Attachment: capacity_sim_may.png (image stub)---

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Julia Connors <julia.connors@cobaltlabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Q2 spike — request for a guaranteed slice + forecast attached

Julia — thanks for the fast turnaround and patience while we scoped this internally. Summary and next steps: 

Decision (temporary MVP): Redwood will offer a forecast-driven preferenced buffer (soft reserved lane) for Cobalt for the two requested windows. Key points:
- We will reserve 8 equivalent slots in a burst lane and allow preemption with 30-min notice.
- Cobalt can submit the forecast file or a signed forecast webhook (legal to approve) — for the first run we will accept the attached spreadsheet and a signed SOW.
- Product will implement a manual autoscale-target bump path (Aditya to scope), infra will pre-assign the burst lane and produce the runbook (Evelyn).
- Ops / commercial will draft terms: pro-rated committed buffer fee + overage billing; legal to review the proposed_slice_terms.pdf (Laura/Dev).

Action owners / ETA:
- Aditya: scope manual forecast ingestion + telemetry events and provide a short implementation plan by Fri May 1 (PROD-6243).
- Evelyn: reserve the 8-slot burst lane for the two windows, produce ops runbook and capacity sim by Mon May 3.
- Laura / Dev: lead commercial T&C updates and send SOW template to Cobalt by Mon May 3.
- Mina: schedule 30-min sync Wed Apr 28 11:00am PT to align on execution (sending calendar invite).

Julia — if that works, I'll have Dev/Laura send the SOW and we can treat this as a paid pilot. If you need a true hard carve with no preemption, we'll need to escalate to finance and legal for committed capacity purchase.

Linking HS record and draft terms: https://hubspot.redwood.com/contacts/HS-4321 and https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-proposed-slice-terms

Thanks all — see you on the sync.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
